statement: On a compact Kähler manifold, every closed positive (1,1)-current T has a global representation T=θ+dd^cφ, where θ is any smooth real closed (1,1)-representative of [T] and φ is a quasi-plurisubharmonic potential. Cao, arXiv:1210.5692v1, Section 2.

statement: If A is a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold X and v is plurisubharmonic on X minus A and locally bounded above near A, then v extends uniquely as a canonical plurisubharmonic function on X. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, Theorem I.5.24.

statement: Two canonical plurisubharmonic functions that agree almost everywhere agree everywhere; consequently the same holds for quasi-plurisubharmonic functions after adding local smooth potentials. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Theorems I.4.18 and I.5.5.

statement: For a positive closed (1,1)-current T, prime divisor D, and rational a≥0 with ν(T,D)≥a, T−a[D] is positive and preserves local rational analytic singularities. DRWNXZ, arXiv:2309.07584v3, Lemma 2.5.

statement: For big ξ on a connected compact Kähler n-fold with a globally smooth connected complete flag, Δ(ξ) is the compact convex closure of gentle analytic Kähler valuations, equivalently rational analytic positive-current valuations near the flag point. Gentle potentials resolve into rational effective divisor poles plus a smooth remainder. For nonbig pseudoeffective ξ, Δ(ξ)=∩ε>0Δ(ξ+ε[ω]). DRWNXZ, Definitions 2.6 and 3.2, Lemma 3.1, Section 3.

statement: For big ξ on a connected compact Kähler n-fold with a globally smooth connected complete flag, n!Vol_RnΔ(ξ)=vol(ξ), where vol(ξ) is the supremum of nonpluripolar top masses of gentle analytic Kähler currents in ξ. Nonbig pseudoeffective classes have volume zero. DRWNXZ, Definition 2.12 and Theorem 7.6.

statement: For closed positive (1,1)-currents T_i=θ_i+dd^cφ_i on a compact Kähler manifold, Cao’s current product pairs a smooth closed complementary-degree form u by lim_j∫∧_i(θ_i+dd^cφ_i,j)_ac∧u, independently of the quasi-equisingular approximations. Such approximations have analytic singularities, converge in L1, have positivity errors tending to zero and monotone singularity order, and satisfy I(m(1+δ)φ_i,j)⊂I(mφ_i) eventually for every positive δ and integer m. Cao, Definitions 2–3.

statement: For a compact Kähler manifold X, its Kähler cone is one connected component of the set of real (1,1)-classes α satisfying ∫Yα^dimY>0 for every positive-dimensional irreducible analytic subset Y⊂X, including X itself. Demailly–Paun, Annals of Mathematics 159 (2004), Main Theorem 0.1.

statement: Let X be a compact Kähler surface, C a smooth compact curve, F a Kähler class, and R∈F|C a Kähler current with finitely many logarithmic poles having rational coefficients and smooth local remainders. The construction in Deng’s Proposition 4.16 extends R to a Kähler current S∈F with S|C=R and rational analytic singularities near those poles when the auxiliary divisorial coefficient is chosen rational. Deng, arXiv:1503.00112v1, Proposition 4.16 and its printed proof.
